newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists mark countdown with street satire.
newsitem.headline: HK activists mark countdown with street satire.

text.p: A handful of human rights activists marked Hong Kong's 100-day countdown to Chinese rule with a street drama on Sunday voicing fears about the future after the handover on June 30.

About 30 people from the Hong Kong People's Alliance for Human Rights, staged a satire at a busy shopping mall in the tourist and shopping district of Tsimshatsui on the tip of the Kowloon peninsula, drawing a small crowd of curious onlookers.
"Hong Kong people will be worried after July 1," organiser and spokeswoman Miranda Yip told reporters.
"Other pro-China groups may celebrate the handover but meanwhile, we think livelihood issues, all the political issues are the main concerns of Hong Kong people," she said.

Hong Kong's vocal pro-democracy lobby fear China's plans to dilute civil liberties laws and dissolve the elected legislature mark the first step towards further snuffing out freedoms in Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years.
More than 7,000 people took to the streets of Hong Kong island to celebrate the impending reunification with the motherland.

"This is a grand and great occasion. In just 100 days, we will return to the Chinese motherland," said chief organiser Raymond Wu at the start of the rally which gathered in Victoria Park -- named after the British queen who reined when Britain, at the height of its imperial powers, seized Hong Kong from China's weak and crumbling Qing dynasty in the mid 19th century.
"We welcome the washing away of over a century of humiliation and shame," Wu said to a burst of applause.
